- **Added npm scripts** for local development:
  - `export:web`: Export the app for web platform
  - `deploy:web`: Export and deploy to EAS Hosting
  - `deploy:web:preview`: Export and deploy with preview settings

## Implementation Details

Both web preview and production deployment jobs:

- Use EAS CLI for deployment to ensure consistency with mobile deployments

items.body:
## Summary
Replaced FlatList with FlashList for improved performance in the photo grid, and added automatic photo refresh when the app returns to foreground to detect newly captured photos.

## Key Changes
- **Switched to FlashList**: Replaced React Native's FlatList with Shopify's FlashList for better performance with large photo grids
- **Added foreground refresh**: Implemented AppState listener to refresh the photo library when the app becomes active, merging new photos without duplicates
- **Extracted PhotoItem component**: Created a memoized PhotoItem component with primitive-only props to optimize re-renders
- **Improved callback stability**: Used useCallback and refs to ensure callbacks maintain stable identities and prevent unnecessary re-renders
- **Enhanced photo merging logic**: New photos are intelligently merged with existing ones, filtering duplicates by ID and maintaining the most recent NUM_PHOTOS items
- **Fixed grid sizing calculation**: Simplified imageSize calculation from `(width - GAP * (NUM_COLUMNS - 1)) / NUM_COLUMNS` to `width / NUM_COLUMNS - GAP`
- **Added scroll-to-bottom on load**: Implemented onContentSizeChange to automatically scroll to the most recent photos on initial load

## Notable Implementation Details
- Photo refresh uses a Set-based deduplication strategy to avoid showing duplicate photos
- The `photosLengthRef` is kept in sync to allow callbacks to read the current photo count without recreating them
- Initial scroll-to-bottom uses `animated: false` to avoid jarring animations
- All callbacks are wrapped with useCallback and use stable refs where needed to maintain referential equality
- Added test coverage for the new photo merging behavior on foreground
- Updated jest.config.js to include @shopify/flash-list in transformIgnorePatterns

items.title: Improve MemeDetailModal dismiss gestures and backdrop interaction
items.body:
## Summary
Enhanced the MemeDetailModal component with improved gesture recognition and user interaction patterns. The changes make dismissing the modal more intuitive through both swipe gestures and backdrop taps, while also improving visual feedback.

## Key Changes
- **Gesture threshold adjustments**: Reduced `DISMISS_THRESHOLD` from 150 to 80 pixels and added velocity-based dismissal (`DISMISS_VELOCITY` of 500) to allow quick flick gestures to close the modal
- **Pan gesture refinement**: Added `activeOffsetY(10)` to the pan gesture to prevent accidental triggers from small vertical movements
- **Backdrop interaction**: Wrapped the backdrop in a `Pressable` component to enable dismissal by tapping outside the modal content
- **Visual improvements**: 
  - Enhanced the swipe indicator with increased size (width: 40→56px, height: 1→1.5px) and opacity (40%→60%)
  - Adjusted padding on the swipe indicator container (pt-3 → pb-1 pt-3)

## Implementation Details
The dismiss logic now uses a compound condition: the modal closes if either the drag distance exceeds the threshold OR the swipe velocity is high enough. This provides a better user experience by allowing both deliberate drags and quick flicks to dismiss the modal. The backdrop is now interactive, allowing users to tap outside the content area to close the modal, which is a common mobile UI pattern.

## Summary
This PR introduces a comprehensive UI component library based on shadcn/ui for React Native, along with a functional photo picker and meme tagging system for the Add screen.

## Key Changes

### UI Component Library
- Added NativeWind (Tailwind CSS for React Native) styling system with global CSS variables and theme configuration
- Implemented core UI components:
  - **Text**: Semantic text component with typography variants (h1-h4, p, blockquote, code, lead, large, small, muted)
  - **Button**: Pressable button with multiple variants (default, destructive, outline, secondary, ghost, link) and sizes
  - **Input**: TextInput wrapper with consistent styling and accessibility features
  - **Badge**: Compact badge component for tags and labels
  - **Card**: Card layout components (Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardContent, CardFooter)
- Added TextClassContext for cascading text styles to child components
- Configured Tailwind with custom color system using CSS variables for light/dark mode support

### Meme Library Context
- Created `MemeLibraryProvider` context for managing meme collection state
- Implemented `useMemeLibrary` hook for accessing meme data and add functionality
- Meme entries include id, uri, tags, and creation timestamp

### Photo Picker & Meme Addition

- Implemented media library permissions handling with user-friendly messaging
- Added `add-meme-modal` screen for tagging photos before saving:
  - Image preview
  - Tag input with add/remove functionality
  - Save button that adds meme to library with tags
- Integrated with Expo Router for modal navigation

### Configuration & Build Setup
- Added Babel configuration with NativeWind preset
- Updated Metro config to process global CSS
- Configured TypeScript paths for cleaner imports
- Updated root layout with theme provider integration and portal host
- Migrated existing screens to use new UI components and Tailwind styling

### Dependencies
- Added `nativewind`, `class-variance-authority`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge` for styling
- Added `@rn-primitives/slot` and `@rn-primitives/portal` for component primitives
- Added `expo-media-library` for photo access

## Notable Implementation Details
- Used CVA (Class Variance Authority) for component variant management
- Implemented platform-specific styling (web vs native) for enhanced web support
- TextClassContext pattern allows parent components to style child Text elements
- Photo grid uses responsive sizing based on window dimensions

items.title: Fixes API Blueprint route's always grouping
items.body:
While using the API Blueprint formatter, I discovered that this gem will always group your endpoint documentation by route no matter what. This isn't always desirable as some users may want to have a bit more control over how these requests are grouped in documentation.

I attempted to write specs:

```ruby
route '/resource/:id', 'Read Resource' do
  get 'fetch resource with specified id' do
    #...
  end
end

route '/resource/:id', 'Update Resource' do
  patch 'update resource with specified id' do
    #...
  end
end
```

as

```ruby
get '/resource/:id' do
  #...
end

post '/resource/:id' do
  #...
end
```

But the test suite will fail with `--format RspecApiDocumentation::ApiFormatter` format because no `route_uri` is set.

I would think that these requests would only be grouped together when they are in the same `route` block but that is not the case. I attempted to adjust functionality to work like that but didn't get very far.

How would you feel about a change like this??? If you want multiple endpoint groupped together they must all have the same route_uri, route_optionals, and route_name?

This means that you can group endpoints as follows

```ruby
route '/resource/:id', 'Read Resource' do
  get 'fetch resource with specified id' do
    #...
  end
end

route '/resource/:id', 'Modify Resource' do
  patch 'update resource with specified id' do
    #...
  end
end

route '/resource/:id', 'Modify Resource' do
  delete 'delete resource with specified id' do
    #...
  end
end
```

This will put the `get` call into it's own "Read Resource" group and the `patch`/`delete` calls into their own "Modify Resource" group.

Another options would be to set something like a "route id" or some kind of unique identifier on the example options [somewhere around here](https://github.com/zipmark/rspec_api_documentation/blob/master/lib/rspec_api_documentation/dsl/resource.rb#L50-L52).

Thoughts? I have no issue updating documentation once we agree on an approach.

items.title: API Blueprint view object respects required: false for parameters now
items.body:
## What Changed
API Blueprint docs now flag `required: false` parameters as optional.

## Why
Default behavior of API Blueprint is to treat all parameters as required unless specified as optional. This change brings the API Blueprint view object more in line with that concept by checking for `required: false` as opposed to setting `required`if `required: true`.

📝 [Upstream PR can be found here](https://github.com/zipmark/rspec_api_documentation/pull/388)

## What Changed
API Blueprint renderer will not flag parameters as `optional` if `required: false` is set

By default, API Blueprint [considers all parameters as required](https://apiblueprint.org/documentation/specification.html#def-uriparameters-section#uri-parameters-section). This change adjusts the API Blueprint view object's logic to set "optional" on a parameter if `required: false` is set.
